channel.title: Security on Validated Patterns
channel.description: Recent content in Security on Validated Patterns

item.title: From Buzzword to Blueprint: Implementing Zero Trust on Red Hat OpenShift with the Layered Zero Trust Validated Pattern
item.description: Zero trust is easy to describe; the hard part is making it repeatable. This fourth article in the ZTVP series steps back from individual security layers to show what a user actually gets when those ideas are assembled into a full, deployable architecture.

item.title: Closing the loop: From network policy intent to verified reality
item.description: Declaring network policy is only half the battle. This post covers common mistakes that undermine network policy intent, the importance of verifying real behavior at runtime, and the design-test-deploy-observe loop that underpins the Zero Trust Validated Pattern.

item.title: Lights On! Real-Time Threat Response with Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security
item.description: When network policies trap an attacker inside a container, what happens next? The ZTVP turns Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security into an active defense engine that detects anomalous behavior and terminates compromised pods in real time.

item.title: Can't Patch Fast Enough? Zero Trust as a Last Line of Defense
item.description: Network policies in the Layered Zero Trust Validated Pattern provide containment when vulnerabilities are discovered faster than patches can be applied. This post introduces the approach and links to the full Red Hat blog article.

item.title: Multicluster DevSecOps
item.description: A validated pattern that uses OpenShift Platform Plus and OpenShift Pipelines to securely build, scan, and deliver applications
